knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A colour change is a variation. It may need more coats and a different price, so it is recorded and approved in writing before painting.
A painting quote states the scope, the system, the coats and the exclusions, so the client knows what the price covers.
Damp repairs found during preparation are excluded unless they are priced as a variation. The brand and coat count are inclusions, not exclusions.
The extra price and the client's approval are recorded in writing before the extra work starts. The NSW guidance on residential building contracts says the same.

practicalCriteria: Given a simulated painting job with a room schedule, the worker writes a quote that states the scope, surfaces, preparation, system, coats, exclusions, colour approval route and validity date.
Given a simulated mid-job request for a darker colour, the worker records a variation with its price and its effect on coats and time, and does not apply the colour until written approval is shown.
The worker records the licence check for the simulated job value and state, with the date and the page checked, before the quote is issued.
passRule: Pass when all three practical criteria are observed by the assessor on the simulated job, with each document complete and signed or approved in the exercise, and no stop-work criterion met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Written quote with scope, exclusions and approval route
Colour approval record with product, colour code or sample reference, and sheen
Variation record with price and written approval
Licence check record for the simulated job
stopWorkCriteria: A colour change or extra work is requested and carried out without written approval
A quote is issued for a job whose licence position has not been checked
A quote is issued without an exclusions section
